Lab Case 1 • Week 3 & Assignment

Lecture 02_ Exploring Data Patterns.xlsx — Vinamilk (VNM) Quarterly Net Revenue (2018 Q1 – 2025 Q2, n = 30)

Unit: Million VND | Source: Vietstock

1. Given Data & Summary Statistics (🇻🇳 Dữ liệu & Thống kê cơ sở)

Sample Size ($n$): $n = 30$ quarters (from 2018 Q1 = $12,120,502$ to 2025 Q2 = $16,724,597$ Million VND).

Sample Mean ($\bar{Y}$): =AVERAGE(C$2:C$31) $= \mathbf{14,706,746.60}$ Million VND.

Denominator ($\sum_{t=1}^{30}(Y_t - \bar{Y})^2$): =DEVSQ(C$2:C$31) $= \mathbf{40,712,769,566,021.20}$.

2. Step-by-Step Lag 1 & Lag 4 Substitution (🇻🇳 Thế số chi tiết tại k=1 và k=4)

At Lag $k=1$: Numerator $= 6,468,882,114,351.04 \implies r_1 = \frac{6.4689\times 10^{12}{4.0713\times 10^{13} = \mathbf{0.158891}$. $SE(r_1) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{30} = \mathbf{0.182574}$, $t_1 = 0.8703 < 1.964$, $Q_1 = 30(32)\frac{0.158891^2}{29} = \mathbf{0.8357}$ ($p = 0.3606$).

At Lag $k=4$ (Quarterly Seasonal Lag!): Numerator $= 22,537,250,727,687.16 \implies r_4 = \mathbf{0.553567}$. Bartlett $SE(r_4) = \sqrt{\frac{1 + 2(0.1589^2 + 0.0513^2 + 0.1321^2)}{30} = \mathbf{0.190673}$. $t_4 = \frac{0.553567}{0.190673} = \mathbf{2.9032 > 1.964}$ (Significant!). Ljung-Box $Q_4 = 1.5469 + 30(32)\frac{0.553567^2}{26} = \mathbf{12.8615 > \chi^2_{0.05,4}=9.4877}$ ($p = \mathbf{0.01197 < 0.05}$).

Analytical Interpretation (🇻🇳 Kết luận & Diễn giải): For lags $k=1, 2, 3$, both individual $|t_k| < 1.964$ and group Ljung-Box $Q_k < \chi^2_{0.05,k}$ ($p > 0.05$), failing to reject $H_0$. However, at Lag $k = 4$, $r_4 = 0.5536$ jumps well above the critical bound ($\pm 0.3745$) and Ljung-Box $Q_4 = 12.8615$ ($p = 0.01197 < 0.05$) strongly rejects $H_0$. This proves Vinamilk's quarterly net revenue exhibits a strong 4-quarter seasonal pattern (peaking every Q2/Q3 summer season and dipping in Q1).
Lab Case 2 • Week 3 Reading

Ljung-Box Test Overview.docx — Residual White-Noise Adequacy Check (n = 100, h = 3)

Q = 7.514 vs χ²_{0.05, 3} = 7.815

Given Data & Step-by-Step Calculation

Given Parameters: Sample size $n = 100$, tested lags $h = 3$, significance level $\alpha = 0.05$ ($5\%$). Residual autocorrelations: $\rho_1 = 0.20$, $\rho_2 = 0.15$, $\rho_3 = -0.10$.

Step 1 (Compute each weighted squared term $\frac{\rho_k^2}{n-k}$):

  • For $k=1$: $0.20^2 / (100 - 1) = 0.04 / 99 \approx 0.0004040$
  • For $k=2$: $0.15^2 / (100 - 2) = 0.0225 / 98 \approx 0.0002296$
  • For $k=3$: $(-0.10)^2 / (100 - 3) = 0.01 / 97 \approx 0.0001031$
  • Total Sum $= 0.0004040 + 0.0002296 + 0.0001031 = \mathbf{0.0007367}$

Q Statistic, Chi-Square Lookup & Conclusion

Step 2 (Compute $Q$): Leading factor $n(n+2) = 100 \times 102 = 10,200$. Therefore:

$$Q = 10,200 \times 0.0007367 \approx \mathbf{7.514}$$

Step 3 (Critical Value): For $df = h = 3$ and $\alpha = 0.05$, $\chi^2_{0.05, 3} = \mathbf{7.815}$.

Step 4 (Conclusion & Interpretation): Since $Q = 7.514 < \chi^2_{0.05, 3} = 7.815$, we fail to reject (accept) $H_0$ at the 5% level. Meaning: The residual series exhibits no statistically significant autocorrelation up to lag 3, satisfying the white-noise adequacy condition of the forecasting model!

Lab Case 3B • Sheet: Moving average (Page 77)

Single Moving Average MA(3) vs. Double Moving Average DMA(3) on Linearly Trending Sales (t = 1..15)

MA(3) MSE = 132.68 vs. DMA(3) MSE = 66.70

Key Insight: Because sales trend steadily upward from $654$ ($t=1$) to $728$ ($t=15$), Single $MA(3)$ suffers positive lag errors in every single period ($e_t > 0$ for all $t=4..15$, MSE $= 132.6759$, forecast $\hat{Y}_{16} = 717$). Double Moving Average $DMA(3)$ corrects this trend lag via $a_t = 2M_t - M'_t$ and $b_t = \frac{2}{3-1}(M_t - M'_t)$, slashing MSE in half to 66.6963 and forecasting $\hat{Y}_{16} = a_{15} + b_{15}(1) = 722 + 5(1) = \mathbf{727}$!

Lab Case 6 • Sheet: Problem 19 (pp.152–153)

Problem 19 — Mt. Spokane Resort Hotel Seasonal Indices & 2007 Monthly Tourist Forecasts

Trend Equation: T^ = 140 + 5t (t=0 is Jan 15, 2001)

Part (a): February 2007 Estimate from January 2007 Actuals

Question: "No sharp cyclical variations are expected during 2007 ($C=1.0, I=1.0$). If 600 tourists were at the resort in January 2007 ($SI_{\text{Jan} = 120$), what is a reasonable estimate for February ($SI_{\text{Feb} = 137$)?"

$$SA_{\text{Jan 2007} = \frac{Y_{\text{Jan}}{S_{\text{Jan}} = \frac{600}{1.20} = 500 \text{ deseasonalized tourists}$$
$$\hat{Y}_{\text{Feb 2007} = SA_{\text{Jan 2007} \times S_{\text{Feb} = 500 \times 1.37 = \mathbf{685 \text{ tourists}$$

(Note: If taking the +5 monthly trend increase from Jan to Feb into account as well, $(500+5)\times 1.37 = 691.85$ tourists, matching Part b!).

Part (c): Average Number of New Tourists Per Month

Question: "What is the average number of new tourists per month?"

Solution: From the linear trend equation $\hat{T}_t = 140 + 5t$, the slope coefficient is $b_1 = \mathbf{+5}$ tourists/month. Therefore, on a deseasonalized trend basis, the resort gains an average of 5 new tourists per month!

Part (b): Forecast for Each Month of 2007 (t = 72..83)

1. Data Pattern Diagnosis, ACF Signatures & Technique Selection Matrix (Ch. 1 & Ch. 2)

Pattern / Property Behavior & Stationarity (🇻🇳 Đặc tính) Correlogram / ACF Signature Appropriate Forecasting Models (Slide L02-S28)
Horizontal (Stationary) Fluctuates around constant mean $\mu$ & constant variance $\sigma^2$ (Dừng) Random: all $r_k \approx 0$ inside $\pm 1.96/\sqrt{n}$. Stationary ARMA: drops to $0$ rapidly after lag 2–3. Simple Naïve, Simple Average, Single MA($k$), Simple Exponential Smoothing (SES), ARMA
Trend (Nonstationary) Persistent long-term growth or decline; mean changes over time (Không dừng) $r_1$ very large (near $+1.0$); slow linear/stepwise decay toward zero across many lags. Remedy: First difference $\Delta Y_t = Y_t - Y_{t-1}$. Naïve Trend, Double Moving Average DMA($k$), Holt's Linear Smoothing, Trend Regression (Linear, Quadratic, Exponential, Growth), ARIMA
Seasonal (Fixed Cycle $s$) Repeats annually at fixed calendar intervals ($s=4$ quarters, $s=12$ months) Significant spikes at seasonal lag $s$ and integer multiples ($k=4, 8, 12$ or $k=12, 24$). Naïve Seasonal / Trend+Seasonal, Winters' Smoothing (Mult/Add), Classical Decomposition, Census X-12/X-11, Seasonal Dummy Regression, SARIMA
Cyclical (> 1 Year) Multi-year wavelike business cycles; variable duration & amplitude Long multi-year sinusoidal swings; hard to isolate without multi-decade data. Classical Decomposition, Business Indicators (Leading [10], Coincident [4], Lagging [7]), Econometric Models, Multiple Regression, ARIMA

2. Complete Mathematical Formula Sheet (Chapters 2, 3 & 4 — All 25 Equations)

Chapter 2: ACF, Hypothesis Tests & Forecast Errors

• Lag-$k$ ACF: $r_k = \frac{\sum_{t=k+1}^n (Y_t - \bar{Y})(Y_{t-k} - \bar{Y})}{\sum_{t=1}^n (Y_t - \bar{Y})^2}$

• Bartlett SE: $SE(r_k) = \sqrt{\frac{1 + 2\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}r_i^2}{n}$  |  White-Noise SE: $SE(r_k) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}$

• Individual $t/Z$ Test: $t_k = \frac{r_k}{SE(r_k)}$, reject $H_0: \rho_k=0$ if $|t_k| > 1.964$ (or $|r_k| > \frac{1.96}{\sqrt{n}$)

• Ljung-Box Portmanteau Test: $Q = n(n+2)\sum_{k=1}^m \frac{r_k^2}{n-k} \sim \chi^2_{df}$ ($df=m$ raw, $m-p-q$ ARIMA). Reject $H_0$ (white noise) if $Q > \chi^2_{\alpha, df}$.

• Residual & Error Metrics: $e_t = Y_t - \hat{Y}_t$  |  $MAD = \frac{\sum |e_t|}{n}$  |  $MSE = \frac{\sum e_t^2}{n}$  |  $RMSE = \sqrt{MSE}$  |  $MAPE = \frac{1}{n}\sum \frac{|e_t|}{|Y_t|}$  |  $MPE = \frac{1}{n}\sum \frac{e_t}{Y_t}$  |  $TS_t = \frac{\sum e_i}{MAD_t}$

Chapter 3: Naïve, Moving Averages & Exponential Smoothing

• 5 Naïve Models: (1) $\hat{Y}_{t+1}=Y_t$; (2) $2Y_t-Y_{t-1}$; (3) $Y_t^2/Y_{t-1}$; (4) $Y_{t-3}$; (5) $Y_{t-3}+\frac{Y_t-Y_{t-4}{4}$

• Updated Simple Avg: $\hat{Y}_{t+2} = \frac{t\hat{Y}_{t+1}+Y_{t+1}{t+1}$  |  Single MA($k$): $M_t = \hat{Y}_{t+1} = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}Y_{t-i}{k}$

• Double MA($k$): $M'_t = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}M_{t-i}{k}$, $a_t = 2M_t - M'_t$, $b_t = \frac{2}{k-1}(M_t - M'_t)$, $\hat{Y}_{t+p} = a_t + b_t p$

• SES: $\hat{Y}_{t+1} = \alpha Y_t + (1-\alpha)\hat{Y}_t = \hat{Y}_t + \alpha e_t$ (Weight on $Y_{t-j}$ is $\alpha(1-\alpha)^j$)

• Holt's Linear: $L_t = \alpha Y_t + (1-\alpha)(L_{t-1}+T_{t-1})$, $T_t = \beta(L_t-L_{t-1})+(1-\beta)T_{t-1}$, $\hat{Y}_{t+p} = L_t + pT_t$ ($L_1=Y_1, T_1=0$ or $Y_2-Y_1$)

• Winters Mult (vs Add): $L_t = \alpha\frac{Y_t}{S_{t-s}+(1-\alpha)(L_{t-1}+T_{t-1})$ [Add: $Y_t-S_{t-s}$]; $T_t = \beta(L_t-L_{t-1})+(1-\beta)T_{t-1}$; $S_t = \gamma\frac{Y_t}{L_t}+(1-\gamma)S_{t-s}$ [Add: $Y_t-L_t$]; $\hat{Y}_{t+p} = (L_t+pT_t)S_{t-s+p}$ [Add: $+S_{t-s+p}$]. Init at $t=s$: $L_s=\bar{Y}_{1..s}$, $T_s=\frac{\sum Y_{s+1..2s}-\sum Y_{1..s}{s^2}$, $S_i=Y_i/L_s$ [Add: $Y_i-L_s$].

Chapter 4: Classical Decomposition, CMA, Seasonal Adjustment & Trend Curves

• Models: Additive $Y_t = T_t + S_t + I_t$ (constant band width, $\sum S_m = 0$) vs. Multiplicative $Y_t = T_t \times C_t \times S_t \times I_t$ (megaphone/funnel spread, $\sum S_m = s$).

• Centered Moving Average (CMA): For $s=4$: $CMA_t = \frac{MA_{t-0.5} + MA_{t+0.5}{2} = \frac{Y_{t-2}+2Y_{t-1}+2Y_t+2Y_{t+1}+Y_{t+2}{8}$ (first at $t=3$). For $s=12$: Two-year moving total $\div 24$ (first at $t=7$).

• Seasonal Index & Normalization: Raw ratio $SI_t = \frac{Y_t}{CMA_t} = S_t \times I_t$. Summarize each season via Median/Mean $\bar{S}_m$, then normalize: $S_m = \bar{S}_m \times \frac{s}{\sum \bar{S}_j}$.

• Seasonal Adjustment (Deseasonalizing): Mult: $SA_t = \frac{Y_t}{S_t} = T_t \times C_t \times I_t$  |  Add: $SA_t = Y_t - S_t$.  |  Cycle-Irregular: $CI_t = \frac{Y_t}{T_t \times S_t}$, $C_t = MA_3(CI_t)$, $I_t = \frac{CI_t}{C_t}$.

• Forecasting Synthesis: $\hat{Y}_{n+p} = \hat{T}_{n+p} \times S_{n+p} \times C \times I$ (with default $C = 1.0, I = 1.0$).  |  Trend Curves: Linear $\hat{T}_t = b_0 + b_1 t$; Quadratic $b_0 + b_1 t + b_2 t^2$; Exponential $b_0 b_1^t$.
